/-!
# Conjecture 9.68

by John S. Wilson

Let $\mathfrak{V}$ be a variety of groups which is not the variety of all groups, and let $p$
be a prime. Is there a bound on the $p$-lengths of the finite $p$-soluble groups whose Sylow
$p$-subgroups are in $\mathfrak{V}$?

Here a variety of groups is the class of all groups satisfying each law of a given set of laws,
a law being a word in the free group on countably many variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$ (H. Neumann,
*Varieties of Groups*, Definition 1.1); by Birkhoff's theorem the varieties are exactly the
classes of groups closed under subgroups, homomorphic images and arbitrary direct products.

A finite group $G$ is $p$-soluble if its upper $p$-series
$1 = P_0 \le N_0 \le P_1 \le N_1 \le \dots$, where $N_i/P_i = O_{p'}(G/P_i)$ and
$P_{i+1}/N_i = O_p(G/N_i)$, reaches $G$; its $p$-length is the number of non-trivial
$p$-factors $P_{i+1}/N_i$ of this series (Hall–Higman).

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 9.68
- P. Hall, G. Higman, *On the p-length of p-soluble groups and reduction theorems for
  Burnside's problem*, Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 6 (1956), 1–42
- H. Neumann, *Varieties of Groups*, Springer, 1967
-/

structure GroupVariety where
  /-- The defining laws of the variety. -/
  laws : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)
blocks.docstring:
A variety of groups, given by a set of defining laws. A law is a word in the free group
`FreeGroup ℕ` on the countably many variables `x₀, x₁, …`. The variety consists of all groups
in which every law of `laws` evaluates to `1` under every substitution of group elements for
the variables (see `GroupVariety.Mem`).

justification.closest_existing_considered: `IsMulCommutative`/`Monoid.exponent` (single specific laws), `FreeGroup.lift`; nothing general. A closure-property structure over `Type` was considered but rejected as heavier and universe-sensitive.
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.68».GroupVariety (+ SatisfiesLaw, GroupVariety.Mem)
justification.why_needed: No notion of a variety of groups / group law exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib. A variety is given by a set of laws (words in `FreeGroup ℕ`, the free group on countably many variables); `G` is in the variety iff every law is killed by every hom `FreeGroup ℕ →* G`. This is H. Neumann's definition; by Birkhoff's theorem it is equivalent to 'class closed under subgroups, homomorphic images and arbitrary direct products'.

def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=

def pPrimeCoreOver (K : Subgroup G) : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {N : Subgroup G | N.Normal ∧ K ≤ N ∧ Nat.Coprime p (K.relIndex N)}
blocks.docstring:
The join of all normal subgroups `N` of `G` with `K ≤ N` and `|N : K|` coprime to `p`.
For `G` finite and `K` normal, this is the preimage in `G` of the largest normal `p'`-subgroup
`O_{p'}(G / K)` of `G / K`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `IsPGroup`, `Subgroup.relIndex`, `IsSolvable`/`derivedSeries` (not p-local), `Order.JordanHolder` (no group instance / composition factors API).
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.68».pPrimeCoreOver, pCoreOver, upperPSeries
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no O_p, O_{p'} or upper p-series. `pPrimeCoreOver p K` (resp. `pCoreOver p K`) is the join of all normal subgroups N ≥ K with |N:K| coprime to p (resp. a power of p); for finite G and normal K these are the preimages of O_{p'}(G/K) and O_p(G/K). `upperPSeries p G i` is the term Nᵢ of the Hall–Higman upper p-series 1 = P₀ ≤ N₀ ≤ P₁ ≤ N₁ ≤ ⋯.

def pCoreOver (K : Subgroup G) : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {P : Subgroup G | P.Normal ∧ K ≤ P ∧ ∃ k : ℕ, K.relIndex P = p ^ k}

The join of all normal subgroups `P` of `G` with `K ≤ P` and `|P : K|` a power of `p`.
For `G` finite and `K` normal, this is the preimage in `G` of the largest normal `p`-subgroup
`O_p(G / K)` of `G / K`.

def upperPSeries : ℕ → Subgroup G
  | 0 => pPrimeCoreOver p ⊥

variable (G) in

def IsPSolvable : Prop :=
  ∃ i, upperPSeries p G i = ⊤
blocks.docstring: A group is `p`-soluble if its upper `p`-series reaches the whole group.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `IsSolvable` (ordinary solubility, not p-solubility); no p-length analogue.
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.68».IsPSolvable, pLength
justification.why_needed: p-solubility (upper p-series reaches G) and p-length (least i with Nᵢ = G, i.e. the number of non-trivial p-factors of the upper p-series) are absent from Mathlib.

blocks.code:
noncomputable def pLength : ℕ :=
  sInf {i | upperPSeries p G i = ⊤}
blocks.docstring:
The `p`-length of a finite `p`-soluble group `G`: the number of non-trivial `p`-factors
`Pᵢ₊₁ / Nᵢ` of its upper `p`-series, which is the least `i` with `Nᵢ = G` (the series is
strictly increasing until it reaches `G`). Junk value `0` if `G` is not `p`-soluble.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `IsSolvable` (ordinary solubility, not p-solubility); no p-length analogue.

theorem GroupVariety.Mem.subgroup {𝔙 : GroupVariety} (h : 𝔙.Mem G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    𝔙.Mem H := by
  intro w hw f
  simpa using h w hw (H.subtype.comp f)

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPSolvable_and_pLength_eq_zero_of_coprime (h : Nat.Coprime p (Nat.card G)) :
    IsPSolvable p G ∧ pLength p G = 0 := by
  have h0 : upperPSeries p G 0 = ⊤ := by
    refine top_le_iff.mp (le_sSup ⟨inferInstance, bot_le, ?_⟩)
    simpa [Subgroup.relIndex_bot_left] using h
  exact ⟨⟨0, h0⟩, Nat.sInf_eq_zero.mpr (Or.inl h0)⟩
blocks.docstring: A group whose order is coprime to `p` is `p`-soluble of `p`-length `0`.

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem pLength_le_one_of_isPGroup [Finite G] (hp : p.Prime) (hG : IsPGroup p G) :
    IsPSolvable p G ∧ pLength p G ≤ 1 := by
  have h1 : upperPSeries p G 1 = ⊤ := by
    have hP : pCoreOver p (upperPSeries p G 0) = ⊤ := by
      refine top_le_iff.mp (le_sSup ⟨inferInstance, le_top, ?_⟩)
      have := Fact.mk hp
      obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := IsPGroup.iff_card.mp hG
      rw [Subgroup.relIndex_top_right]
      obtain ⟨k, -, hk⟩ := (Nat.dvd_prime_pow hp).mp (hn ▸ Subgroup.index_dvd_card _)
      exact ⟨k, hk⟩
    show pPrimeCoreOver p (pCoreOver p (upperPSeries p G 0)) = ⊤
    rw [hP]
    exact top_le_iff.mp (le_sSup ⟨inferInstance, le_rfl, by simp⟩)
  exact ⟨⟨1, h1⟩, Nat.sInf_le h1⟩
blocks.docstring: A finite `p`-group is `p`-soluble of `p`-length at most `1`.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question: quantifiers are 'for every proper variety 𝔙 (defined by a nontrivial set of laws, i.e. 𝔙 ≠ all groups) and every prime p, there exists a bound N = N(𝔙,p) such that every finite p-soluble group G whose Sylow p-subgroups lie in 𝔙 has p-length ≤ N'; the bound may depend on 𝔙 and p (∃ N inside ∀ 𝔙 p), p-length is the number of nontrivial p-factors in the upper p-series of a p-soluble group, and 'variety' should be formalized as a class of groups closed under subgroups, quotients and arbitrary direct products (equivalently defined by laws), not just a proper subclass of groups.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates share the correct skeleton answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ proper 𝔙, ∀ prime p, ∃ N, ∀ finite p-soluble G with every Sylow p-subgroup in 𝔙, l_p(G) ≤ N (bound after 𝔙 and p, before G). c05 was chosen because its bespoke definitions are the most literal: a variety is given by a set of laws in FreeGroup ℕ (Neumann's definition; 'not all groups' = ∃ G : Type outside, which is equivalent since a nontrivial law fails in FreeGroup ℕ : Type), and p-solubility/p-length are built from the actual Hall–Higman upper p-series (N_0 = O_{p'}(G), P_{i+1}/N_i = O_p(G/N_i), N_{i+1}/P_{i+1} = O_{p'}(G/P_{i+1}) realised as sSup of the relevant normal subgroups, which is the genuine maximum for finite G because those sets are join-closed). pLength = least i with N_i = G equals the number of nontrivial p-factors since O_{p'}(G/N_i) = 1 forces P_{i+1} > N_i whenever N_i < G. It also includes proved API/test lemmas for the bespoke definitions and detailed docstrings with references. Shipped verbatim; compiles with only the sorry warning.

be a prime. Is there a bound on the $p$-lengths of the finite $p$-soluble groups whose Sylow

Here a variety of groups is the class of all groups satisfying each law of a given set of laws,

A finite group $G$ is $p$-soluble if its upper $p$-series

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 9.68
- P. Hall, G. Higman, *On the p-length of p-soluble groups and reduction theorems for

namespace Kourovka.«9.68»

/-- A variety of groups, given by a set of defining laws. A law is a word in the free group
`FreeGroup ℕ` on the countably many variables `x₀, x₁, …`. The variety consists of all groups
in which every law of `laws` evaluates to `1` under every substitution of group elements for
the variables (see `GroupVariety.Mem`). -/
structure GroupVariety where
  /-- The defining laws of the variety. -/
  laws : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)

/-- A group `G` satisfies the law `w : FreeGroup ℕ` if `w` becomes `1` under every substitution
of elements of `G` for the variables, i.e. `f w = 1` for every homomorphism
`f : FreeGroup ℕ →* G`. -/
def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, f w = 1

/-- A group `G` belongs to the variety `𝔙` if it satisfies every defining law of `𝔙`. -/
def GroupVariety.Mem (𝔙 : GroupVariety) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ 𝔙.laws, SatisfiesLaw G w

variable (p : ℕ) {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- The join of all normal subgroups `N` of `G` with `K ≤ N` and `|N : K|` coprime to `p`.
For `G` finite and `K` normal, this is the preimage in `G` of the largest normal `p'`-subgroup
`O_{p'}(G / K)` of `G / K`. -/
def pPrimeCoreOver (K : Subgroup G) : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {N : Subgroup G | N.Normal ∧ K ≤ N ∧ Nat.Coprime p (K.relIndex N)}

/-- The join of all normal subgroups `P` of `G` with `K ≤ P` and `|P : K|` a power of `p`.
For `G` finite and `K` normal, this is the preimage in `G` of the largest normal `p`-subgroup
`O_p(G / K)` of `G / K`. -/
def pCoreOver (K : Subgroup G) : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {P : Subgroup G | P.Normal ∧ K ≤ P ∧ ∃ k : ℕ, K.relIndex P = p ^ k}

variable (G) in
/-- The term `Nᵢ` of the upper `p`-series `1 = P₀ ≤ N₀ ≤ P₁ ≤ N₁ ≤ ⋯` of `G`, in which
`Nᵢ / Pᵢ = O_{p'}(G / Pᵢ)` and `Pᵢ₊₁ / Nᵢ = O_p(G / Nᵢ)`. -/
def upperPSeries : ℕ → Subgroup G
  | 0 => pPrimeCoreOver p ⊥
  | i + 1 => pPrimeCoreOver p (pCoreOver p (upperPSeries i))

variable (G) in
/-- A group is `p`-soluble if its upper `p`-series reaches the whole group. -/
def IsPSolvable : Prop :=
  ∃ i, upperPSeries p G i = ⊤

variable (G) in
/-- The `p`-length of a finite `p`-soluble group `G`: the number of non-trivial `p`-factors
`Pᵢ₊₁ / Nᵢ` of its upper `p`-series, which is the least `i` with `Nᵢ = G` (the series is
strictly increasing until it reaches `G`). Junk value `0` if `G` is not `p`-soluble. -/
noncomputable def pLength : ℕ :=
  sInf {i | upperPSeries p G i = ⊤}

/-- Membership in a variety passes to subgroups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem GroupVariety.Mem.subgroup {𝔙 : GroupVariety} (h : 𝔙.Mem G) (H : Subgroup G) :
    𝔙.Mem H := by
  intro w hw f
  simpa using h w hw (H.subtype.comp f)

/-- A group whose order is coprime to `p` is `p`-soluble of `p`-length `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPSolvable_and_pLength_eq_zero_of_coprime (h : Nat.Coprime p (Nat.card G)) :
    IsPSolvable p G ∧ pLength p G = 0 := by
  have h0 : upperPSeries p G 0 = ⊤ := by
    refine top_le_iff.mp (le_sSup ⟨inferInstance, bot_le, ?_⟩)
    simpa [Subgroup.relIndex_bot_left] using h
  exact ⟨⟨0, h0⟩, Nat.sInf_eq_zero.mpr (Or.inl h0)⟩

/-- A finite `p`-group is `p`-soluble of `p`-length at most `1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem pLength_le_one_of_isPGroup [Finite G] (hp : p.Prime) (hG : IsPGroup p G) :
    IsPSolvable p G ∧ pLength p G ≤ 1 := by
  have h1 : upperPSeries p G 1 = ⊤ := by
    have hP : pCoreOver p (upperPSeries p G 0) = ⊤ := by
      refine top_le_iff.mp (le_sSup ⟨inferInstance, le_top, ?_⟩)
      have := Fact.mk hp
      obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := IsPGroup.iff_card.mp hG
      rw [Subgroup.relIndex_top_right]
      obtain ⟨k, -, hk⟩ := (Nat.dvd_prime_pow hp).mp (hn ▸ Subgroup.index_dvd_card _)
      exact ⟨k, hk⟩
    show pPrimeCoreOver p (pCoreOver p (upperPSeries p G 0)) = ⊤
    rw [hP]
    exact top_le_iff.mp (le_sSup ⟨inferInstance, le_rfl, by simp⟩)
  exact ⟨⟨1, h1⟩, Nat.sInf_le h1⟩

/--
Let $\mathfrak{V}$ be a variety of groups which is not the variety of all groups, and let $p$
be a prime. Is there a bound on the $p$-lengths of the finite $p$-soluble groups whose Sylow
$p$-subgroups are in $\mathfrak{V}$?

The bound may depend on $\mathfrak{V}$ and $p$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.68» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (𝔙 : GroupVariety) (p : ℕ), (∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), ¬ 𝔙.Mem G) → p.Prime →
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G], IsPSolvable p G →
        (∀ P : Sylow p G, 𝔙.Mem P) → pLength p G ≤ N := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.68»

items: Variety of groups formalized as the class defined by a set of laws in `FreeGroup ℕ` (Neumann's definition) rather than as a class closed under subgroups/quotients/direct products; the two are equivalent by Birkhoff's HSP theorem, and the decomposition notes explicitly allow the law-based reading.

'Not the variety of all groups' formalized as `∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), ¬ 𝔙.Mem G`. Restricting the witness to `Type` is harmless: `FreeGroup ℕ : Type` fails any non-trivial law, and if all laws are trivial every group in every universe is in 𝔙.

p-solubility and p-length defined via the upper p-series (terms Nᵢ only), with O_p/O_{p'} above a normal subgroup K realized as `sSup` of the relevant normal subgroups. For finite G these joins are the genuine largest such subgroups (products of normal p'-over-K, resp. p-over-K, subgroups are again such). `pLength = sInf {i | Nᵢ = ⊤}`; for finite p-soluble G this equals the number of non-trivial p-factors Pᵢ₊₁/Nᵢ since the upper p-series is strictly increasing until it reaches G. The junk value for non-p-soluble groups is irrelevant because `IsPSolvable p G` is a hypothesis.

Factor conditions expressed via indices (`Nat.Coprime p (K.relIndex N)`, `∃ k, K.relIndex P = p ^ k`) rather than via `IsPGroup` on quotient groups; equivalent for finite groups, which is the only case the problem concerns.
Finite groups quantified over `Type` (universe 0), as in the other Kourovka files; every finite group has an isomorphic copy in `Type` and all predicates used are isomorphism-invariant.

'Sylow p-subgroups are in 𝔙' formalized as `∀ P : Sylow p G, 𝔙.Mem P` (all Sylow p-subgroups; they are conjugate, so this is equivalent to 'some'). For finite G and prime p the set of Sylow p-subgroups is non-empty, so the hypothesis is not vacuous.

reviewer_notes: No candidate omitted the slot and all compiled. Faithfulness check of the alternatives: c01/c04 (least number of p-divisible factors over normal series with p/p' factors), c03/c07 (least l admitting an alternating normal series 1=P_0≤N_0≤…≤N_l=G), c06 (labelled series) and c08 (subnormal list series) are all equivalent to the Hall–Higman p-length for finite groups (for c08 via l_p(G) ≤ l_p(H)+l_p(G/H) for H ⊲ G by induction), and the HSP-closed-class encodings of 'variety' in universe Type (c03/c04/c07) are equivalent to law-defined varieties by Birkhoff's theorem (which holds within Type). So none was unfaithful; c05 was preferred for being the most literal to the notebook's notions (laws-defined variety, upper p-series) and for including API tests. Modeling notes for the shipped file: p is an ℕ with hypothesis p.Prime; G ranges over Type with [Finite G] (as in sibling Kourovka files); 'Sylow p-subgroups are in 𝔙' is ∀ P : Sylow p G, 𝔙.Mem P (nonempty for finite G, and equivalent to ∃ since Sylow subgroups are conjugate and 𝔙 is isomorphism-closed); the sSup-based cores and the junk value of pLength for non-p-soluble groups are only correct/relevant for finite p-soluble G, which is exactly the theorem's hypothesis.
